headline: Maui County Council Meeting

meeting.summary: The Council honored Maui County Fair volunteers and passed bills on safe parking, tax exemptions, budget grants and an Aloha Classic sponsor change.
meeting.recap: A resolution honored generations of volunteers and groups who helped build the Maui County Fair.[[0:16:45]] The fair resolution passed with nine ayes and zero noes.[[0:28:19]] A testifier cited a 2023 state study: 27% of middle schoolers statewide seriously considered suicide.[[0:46:40]] A resolution urged state education and health departments to partner with the County and a wildfire study on school mental health services.[[1:00:21]] Bill 133 would allow more flexibility in the hours and conditions of each safe parking site.[[1:11:45]] A County director said the temporary site will run 24 hours, with a shuttle to the transit hub.[[1:21:56]] Bill 134 would let the mayor sign a water monitoring agreement with the U.S. Geological Survey through September 30, 2027.[[1:30:30]] Bill 135 fixes a real property tax exemption reference that was left out by mistake.[[1:38:19]] Bills 136 and 137 passed first reading with eight ayes, zero noes, and one member excused.[[1:44:10]] The October 23rd meeting will be held in chambers.[[1:47:03]]
meeting.next: A County director said staff will help safe parking participants get an ID or driver's license.

issues.oneLine: Bill 134 would let the mayor sign a water monitoring agreement with the U.S. Geological Survey.
issues.why: The program collects rainfall, streamflow, and groundwater data used to track Maui County water resources on Maui and Molokaʻi.
issues.brief: The agreement covers October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027.[[#1]] The agreement would cost $225,920, with $199,720 from the Department of Water Supply and $26,200 from the U.S. Geological Survey.[[#2]]

issues.oneLine: Bill 137 adds a $75,000 state Department of Health grant for a farmers market navigator program.
issues.why: The budget director said the program will support participating farmers markets.
issues.brief: The grant goes to the Department of Agriculture from the state's Chronic Disease Prevention Health Promotion Division.[[#1]] Bill 137 passed first reading with eight ayes and zero noes.[[#2]]

issues.oneLine: A resolution urged state education and health departments to partner with the County and the Maui Wildfire Exposure Study on school mental health services.
issues.why: The resolution says the study examines how the 2023 Maui wildfires affect survivors' physical and mental health, child development, and recovery.
issues.brief: A testifier cited a 2023 state study finding 27% of middle schoolers statewide seriously considered suicide.[[#1]] The resolution seeks a simple, voluntary mental health screening and referral pathway for children in Maui County schools.[[#2]] The resolution encourages the state departments to name representatives to build an implementation plan with the County.[[#3]] A vote was called on the resolution, but the result is not in the captions.[[#4]]
